title: Papua New Guinea

endonym.native: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

capsule: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea together with numerous offshore island groups, and from 1884 was divided between German New Guinea (northeast) and British Papua (southeast), both eventually administered by Australia after World War I. Australia governed the territory under a United Nations trust arrangement after 1946 and granted independence on 16 September 1975, making Papua New Guinea one of the world's most linguistically diverse nations, with over 800 distinct languages. The country holds extensive mineral and hydrocarbon resources — gold, copper, and liquefied natural gas — but the benefits have been unevenly distributed, and large parts of the Highlands remain outside effective state administration. Papua New Guinea joined the Commonwealth and established constitutional parliamentary government at independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Papua New Guinea's international boundaries are defined by treaty and fully attested; the land border with Indonesian Papua (formerly Irian Jaya) follows the 141°E meridian with minor surveyed deviations.
